cohort: The study included 11 male fetuses from 6 French families with antenatally diagnosed Tonne-Kalscheuer syndrome (TOKAS) due to RLIM variations.
finding: The study significantly extended the phenotypical spectrum and known genotype of fetal TOKAS, identifying a high frequency of diaphragmatic hernia, differences in sex development, and various visceral malformations, alongside a recurrent p.(Arg611Cys) variant accounting for 66% of fetal cases.
